newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes stricter rule on forex assets.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes stricter rule on forex assets.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Monday the Monetary Board was studying the possibility of imposing a stricter rule on banks' foreign exchange assets to make them more liquid.
"We may require them to hold part of their foreign currency assets in foreign banks' (cash) balances and readily marketable securities," Singson told reporters after attending an investors' forum.
He declined to say when the board will act on the proposal or how much foreign exchange assets should be kept by banks in cash and marketable securities.
"It's just like an additional precautionary move," he said, in response to a query whether the proposal was being considered because some banks have over-extended their foreign exchange loans.
Banks' foreign exchange liabilities are currently required to be 100 percent covered by foreign exchange assets.
Singson said most of the foreign exchange loans were given to exporters who can easily source their loan payment from their earnings.
At present, about 50 percent of banks' foreign exchange assets are in long-term loans, he said.
The Philippine banking industry was recently hit by speculations that banks have overextended their foreign exchange loans and may suffer the same crisis that crippled Thailand's financial market.
